newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta call money traded at 8.0/9.0 percent.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta call money traded at 8.0/9.0 percent.

text.p: Jakarta call money was traded at 8.0/9.0 percent on Tuesday morning on sufficient supply.
Dealers said liquidity was ample, driving short-term rates and forward points down across the board.
One foreign bank dealer said early central bank supply of 354 billion rupiah, aided by government transfers of civil servants salaries, helped keep the market flush.
But longer-term rates were firm, with one-month money quoted at 14.00/14.25 and three-month at 14.5/14.75 percent, respectively.
The average overnight interbank rate on Monday was 9.92 percent, compared with 13.22 percent on Friday.
One bond dealer said prices were stable despite some selling from offshore investors due to election campaign jitters.
"We have brisk demand from local mutual funds to absorb offshore unloading," he said.
